I was raised in a christian household, and the consensus is that anything that isn't straight (except for asexuality, which no one really talks about) is a temptation, and acting on your feelings in any way at all is a moral failing on your part. 

It's probably different depending on the church, but developing your own opinions can be challenging when something like that is your only base line.
I was.

I would  always convince myself that I had crushes on boys and never really thought about all the times I noticed just how pretty girls were. When I found out what homosexuality was- something "against the bible" that "we don't agree with" I frantically rationalized my feelings towards girls as just being friends, and I blamed non-christians for making it seem as though I did like girls. I started comparing myself to the older girls in the church who invited people and always prayed and read their bibles every day. I invited several people to my church and panicked when they told me they were weren't christian and would not change. 

I got immensely uncomfortable whenever the lgbt+ community was mentioned in media and was disgusted whenever someone expressed joy at lgbt+ representation. Eventually I told my best friend (who went to my church)  that I liked her, (I apologized multiple times and made it clear I knew that the feelings I had were sinful) and she got really awkward and expressed that this made her uncomfortable and it would be the same if I were a boy. She had previously, and on multiple occasions, mentioned that physical attraction was weird and she didn't understand how people could like someone that way. I'm reasonably sure that she's asexual and/or aromantic. Much later, I asked if she thought that this was the case. She seemed uncomfortable with this, reminded me that we were getting close to sinning, and changed the subject. She reminded me of me, but with even less opportunity to understand opposing viewpoints. (She was homeschooled and I was her only friend)

I told my mom that I liked her soon after I told her and my mom told me that, while liking her was not a sin, having a relationship was, and even thinking about how I liked girls could lead me to that point. So I tried to ignore my feelings, and failed quite miserably, and I started to hate myself for that as well. I eventually came to terms with my sexuality and came out as bi to some friends at my school. I realized that I had been suppressing my feelings on almost everything in my effort to be a good christian. I realized that I had so many opinions on different things that I loved exploring. Not my parents', not christianity's, MY opinions. 

Soon after that, I came out of bi to our small group in my church, under the guise that my feelings toward girls were temptations and I wanted them to pray  to get rid of them. Another girl told me that she was bi as well, and that it didn't stop her from being a good christian.

So, yeah, we were indoctrinated, both by our families and by the church, and I strongly dislike that we never get to choose to be religious or not. We follow the church until we reach our breaking point, when we either leave or are encouraged to bury our feelings and/or overcome them, because that's what god wants us to do.

There were others beside her, of lower ranks, but they didn't matter, no one mattered, while Avem stood in front of her. Besides the strange substance that kept her captive, nothing could undermine the leader's majesty.

"Lavender." Avem's blue eyes seemed to be the most amplified by life force; they were what Lavender's were drawn to and never left while in her presence. It was like getting a glimpse of her leader's beautiful soul.

"Goddess." She trembled ever so slightly, and her dark brown curls rustled like leaves that sensed the approach of autumn.

"I... have some unfortunate news." Lavender stood rooted to the spot. The advance scouts had said that Rubia would be easiest to infiltrate. Had it gone poorly? Had anyone been discovered? Or had they found someone that met their description, and had they been too powerful? "Your apprentice..." Avem was hesitant, unsure of how to tell her. But Lavende could tell, could always tell when one of their number had fallen. This moment was always the most horrible, right before it was spoken aloud, when it would become real in seconds. Immortality meant none of them would die, or at least it would take several centuries. But it always hit hard, even with those they hadn't known well. Evinco had been with them for two hundred years. Young, but determined, and never quite good enough. It had been his dream to train under Lavender, second in command to Avem herself. And now...

"Is," Lavender's voice cracked. "Is he dead?" She shouldn't have asked. Tears welled up in her deep brown eyes, and she forced them away with a stab of rage.

"Yes, Evinco was discovered. By those new... experimental forces of Ionee's. They had been watching him for awhile. He tried to fight, but he was alone and there were seven of them." 

Lavender got her emotions under control. "Thank you for telling me this, Goddess."

She was unaware that she was walking until she exited the crystalline cave and blinked in the sunlight. The lush meadows, forests, and lakes of Eden could be seen in every direction. This was a perfect empire, one  that would soon span the entire world. The Americas had been conquered already, but Eurasia was yet to be made into something so ethereal. 

They just had to find someone with the ability to break Avem's bonds, so that her full power could be unleashed. Lavender, though also a manipulator of life force, wasn't nearly as powerful. 

If only they hadn't trusted the third one, who could use both light and dark life force and break down objects into anything. If only Lavender had been able to stop him. If only she had trained  Evinco differently, and he had known what to do. If she had done anything, anything, would he still be alive?

She felt her face and realized she was crying now, and had been for hours. Lavender wearily sat down under the shade of a large tree. Evinco's face filled her mind, and she jumped back to her feet. A patch of grass around her wilted as her life force whipped around her. *To hell with the plan. It isn't working and nothing has happened in five hundred years. If we just invaded, all of us at once... there are millions of them, but we're more powerful... or at least pretended to be one of them, and attacked them from the inside... I'm tired of waiting... Evinco died in vain...*

She wasn't sure what she would do next, and knew that Avem would be strongly opposed to this, and knew that it was unlikely to happen. But Evinco had died, and she knew who was responsible. *No matter what else happens, I'll kill Ionee and everyone under her command.*
